quote: Theorem 2: Let X1 ~ APTQLD(α1, β1, θ1) and X2 ~ APTQLD(α2, β2, θ2). If α1 < α2, β1 = β2 = β and θ1 = θ2 = θ, then X1 ≤lr X2. ... quote: X1 is smaller than X2 in: a) stochastic order (X1 ≤st X2) if R1(x,α1,β1,θ1) ≤ R2(x,α2,β2,θ2); b) hazard rate order (X1 ≤hr X2) if h1(x,α1,β1,θ1)/h2(x,α2,β2,θ2) is decreasing in x; c) mean residual life order (X1 ≤mrl X2) if E(X1−t|X1<t) ≤ E(X2−t|X2<t); d) likelihood ratio order (X1 ≤lr X2) if f1(x,α1,β1,θ1)/f2(x,α2,β2,θ2) is a decreasing function of x. Notably, if (X1 ≤lr X2), then (X1 ≤hr X2), (X1 ≤mrl X2) and (X1 ≤st X2).
